title: The Last Bid
logline: At a dawn fish auction, a buyer who comes every morning for a particular catch loses it, again, to a higher bid.
human_question: What is it like to want something you can never quite outbid?

situation.what_happens: Each morning a catch is landed and sold within an hour, in fast public bidding among buyers who all know one another. One buyer comes for the same thing every day, with a limit set by what they can sell it on for. On a good morning they get it. On this one, somebody with more room goes past their limit and the lot is gone in seconds. They will be back tomorrow with the same limit.
situation.who_is_involved: Buyers who resell, each with a ceiling set by their own customers; the crews whose night's work is being priced in front of them; the auctioneer; the families on both sides of every price.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the buyer, a day's trade and a customer who expects that fish. For the crew, whether the night paid for itself. For the higher bidder, very little. The source's own caution matters here: earning a living is not treated as a fault, so the buyer cannot be used as an exhibit of greed.
situation.how_it_unfolds: An auction morning is over almost as soon as it starts and repeats the next day without memory: boats in, lots called, prices set by how much was landed and who turned up, everyone gone by mid-morning. Across a season the same buyer wins some and loses more. Whether they raise their limit, hold it, or stop coming is theirs to decide, and any single lot is settled in seconds by somebody else.

concept_merge.why_together: C005 contributes the occasion and its limit: earning, guarding and spending are listed among the everyday occasions of greed-rooted minds, while the same work done with regard to what is useful is explicitly not counted as unwholesome, so a working buyer is exactly the case the sources refuse to settle from outside. C021 contributes the forces in the room: effort, defined as what does not turn back until a task is done, and decision, which settles firmly on something whether or not it is right, neither of them carrying any moral colour of its own.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That resolve and wanting are not the same thing even when they arrive in the same person in the same second, and that a decision can be complete, firm and wrong. Closing on a refusal delivered by somebody else's stronger want, it shows the wall the whole group has been moving towards: nothing was taken, nothing was unfair, and the wanting simply stopped.

concept_links.why: Earning, guarding and spending wealth are among the source's everyday occasions for greed-rooted minds [C005-M:L5] [C005-M:L7], and the same source says the same work done with practical wisdom, with regard to what is useful, is not counted as unwholesome [C005-M:L9]. A buyer trading for a living sits on that line, and the film must leave them on it rather than deciding for them.

Effort is described as the mental quality that does not turn back until a task is done, and decision (adhimokkha) as the mind settling firmly on an object whether or not it is right [C021-M:L19] [C021-P:L45]; both are named as morally neutral factors that take the colour of the mind they join. The digest notes the sources disagree on how discernible decision is, one calling it hard to detect and the other stressing how often it is wrong [C021-M:L15] [C021-P:L45], so the film should show the moment of deciding without claiming to read it.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Coming back every morning takes effort and resolve, and the texts say effort is not the same as greed. When somebody else bids higher, even a well-practised wanting simply hits a wall.
what_must_be_real: A real auction, real buyers and a real outcome. No bid arranged, no limit disclosed on anyone's behalf, and no loss re-enacted.
position_hint: closing candidate: the group's last beat, where wanting is refused not by bad luck or an official but by somebody else's stronger want, which is what hands the group on.
risks: Provoking or exploiting a losing buyer's frustration
Using a working trader as an exhibit of greed, which the sources themselves refuse
Commercial sensitivity around prices and limits
Spectacle standing in for one person's real stake
drop_if: No buyer with a genuine, repeated stake will take part over more than one morning
The outcome can only be shown by arranging a bid

connections.note: One person loses what they never quite got; the held idea has a family losing what they finally had.
Two refusals: one delivered by a system that meant nothing by it, one by another person wanting the same thing more.

selection.reason: Closes the group on wanting refused by a stronger want, with effort and decision kept clearly apart from greed.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
